title: Reduced identity components of closed abelian subgroups
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $A/k$ be an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety], and let $H\hookrightarrow A$ be a closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Then $H_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a subgroup scheme, and its connected component $B=(H_{\mathrm{red}})^0$ containing the identity is an abelian variety, embedded as a closed subgroup of $A$. One has $\dim B=\dim H$. In particular, if $\dim B=0$, the structure morphism $H\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite, including when $H$ is nonreduced.

source.place: Corollary 1.35 and discussion before Proposition 1.37 (components and dimension), Proposition 1.38 and Corollary 1.39 (reduced subgroup over a perfect field); smoothness of reduced groups: Stacks groupoids.tex Tag 047P, lemma-reduced-group-scheme-prefect-field-characteristic-p-smooth, and its characteristic-zero companion; Milne AV I Proposition 8.1 uses this abelian subvariety.

proof.text: By [def-sc-abelian-variety], $A$ is proper over $k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] first to $H\hookrightarrow A$, and then to the reduction $i:G=H_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow H$ of [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism]. Thus $H$ and $G$ are proper, hence of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Since $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian (a field has only the ideals $0$ and $k$), [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $G$ Noetherian. The reduction node gives reducedness of $G$.

The field $k$ is perfect: in positive characteristic every $a\in k$ has a $p$th root because $T^p-a$ has a root; characteristic zero is the other case in [lem-kun-geometric-reduced-perfect]. That node applied to the reduced finite-type scheme $G$ gives geometric reducedness and flatness over $k$. Apply [lem-sfb-flat-geometrically-reduced-pullback] with $Y=T=G$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$. The hypotheses are exactly the preceding geometric reducedness and flatness, and the reduced locally Noetherian property from step 1. Thus $G\times_kG$ is reduced.

source.place: Tags 020I/035Z, lemma-perfect-reduced and lemma-geometrically-reduced-any-base-change; the hint in groupoids.tex Tag 047R

proof.text: Restrict the multiplication of $H$ along $i\times i:G\times_kG\to H\times_kH$. Its reduced source from step 2 lets [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] factor this map to $H$ through $i:G\to H$. The same statement factors the inverse restricted to $G$ and the unit from the reduced scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$. These restrictions satisfy the group axioms: composing either side of each associativity, unit or inverse identity with $i$ gives the corresponding identity in $H$. A closed immersion is a monomorphism (on affine opens a map into its quotient ring, if it exists, is uniquely determined), so those equalities hold in $G$. Thus $G$ is a group scheme and $i$ a homomorphism. Together with $H\hookrightarrow A$, this proves the reduced-subgroup clause.

source.place: Proposition 1.38 and Corollary 1.39, printed p.18; groupoids.tex Tag 047R, lemma-reduced-subgroup-scheme-perfect, with its omitted details expanded

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-group-neutral-component-translates] to the finite-type group scheme $G$. Its identity component $B$ is a connected open subscheme and a closed subgroup scheme of $G$. Step 2 supplies the hypothesis of [lem-sfb-geometrically-reduced-group-smooth], so $G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](a) with source open $B$ and the entire target to obtain smoothness of $B$.

source.place: Tag 0B7R, proposition-connected-component; Tags 047N/047P, smoothness; morphisms.tex Tag 01V6, lemma-smooth-characterize

proof.text: The closed immersion $B\hookrightarrow G$ and properness of $G$ imply properness of $B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Together with connectedness and smoothness from step 4, [def-sc-abelian-variety] says precisely that $B$ is an abelian variety. The three closed immersions $B\hookrightarrow G\hookrightarrow H\hookrightarrow A$ compose to a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-products], and their group homomorphisms compose. Thus this is the required closed abelian subgroup of $A$.

source.place: Tags 01W3/01W5, proper closed subschemes; definition of abelian variety in groupoids.tex Tag 03RO

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-group-neutral-component-translates], $G$ is a finite disjoint union of clopen components, each isomorphic to $B$. Every irreducible closed subset of $G$ lies in one component: meeting a clopen component and its complement would disconnect it. Consequently every strict chain of nonempty irreducible closed subsets lies in one component. The supremum of these chain lengths is therefore $\dim B$, by [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and the translation isomorphisms; $B$ is itself a component. The homeomorphism $|G|\to|H|$ supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism] carries these chains bijectively, so $\dim H=\dim G=\dim B$. This uses the topology and does not discard nilpotents by assuming $H$ reduced.

source.place: Corollary 1.35 and dimension discussion before Proposition 1.37, printed p.17; reduction homeomorphism: Stacks Tag 054M

proof.text: If $\dim B=0$, step 6 gives $\dim H=0$ for the topological Krull dimension. Since $H$ is nonempty (it has the unit point), [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] identifies this with $\sup_{x\in H}\dim\mathcal O_{H,x}$, so $\dim H=0$ also in the sense of [def-pc-dimension] used by the next node. Step 1 established properness of $H$ without any reducedness assumption. Apply [lem-pc-dim-zero-finite-over-field] to this proper zero-dimensional $k$-scheme $H$. It gives that $H\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite, including the nonreduced case.
